prompt: The new chat tool made the team reply faster, so managers expected faster replies, so the team added a status feature to show when they're busy.
tells: so the team added a status feature
why: The tool changed habits, the habits changed expectations, and that led to changing the tool. Tools and work shaping each other over time.
trap: It isn't only one number driving behaviour; there's a back-and-forth with the tool.

prompt: The ward changed its handover routine to fit the new tablets, then asked IT to change the tablet screens to fit the new routine.
tells: then asked IT to change the tablet screens
why: First the routine adapted to the tool, then the tool was adapted to the routine. That back and forth is tools and work shaping each other.
trap: They aren't going around the tablets; both the routine and the tablets changed.

prompt: As email made it easy to copy everyone, people started writing for a crowd, and the company then added a 'reply all' warning.
tells: the company then added a 'reply all' warning
why: Email changed how people wrote, which then led to changing email. Neither caused the other alone; they shaped each other.
trap: The warning is a built-in rule, but the clue is the cycle of changes on both sides.

prompt: Farmers changed how they plant to fit the new machines, and the makers then redesigned the machines around how farmers worked.
tells: the makers then redesigned the machines around how farmers worked
why: Machines changed farming and farming changed the machines in turn. That mutual change over time is shaping each other.
trap: It isn't stuck; both sides kept adjusting.

prompt: Video calls changed how meetings run, people began keeping cameras off, and the tool then added avatars and reactions in response.
tells: the tool then added avatars and reactions in response
why: Use changed the tool and the tool changed use, back and forth. That's tools and practice shaping each other.
trap: One group's different use isn't the point; the tool and habits co-evolved.

prompt: The team's board started with three columns, their way of working changed, they added columns, and the new columns changed how they work again.
tells: the new columns changed how they work again
why: The board and the team's habits kept adjusting to each other. Neither simply caused the other; they shaped each other.
trap: The columns don't enforce one fixed rule; they evolve with the work.
